name: Comparison Slider
blurb: Two versions of one picture stacked exactly on top of each other, with a divider you drag across them. The line does not snap to the pointer - a critically damped spring pulls it there, so a flick throws it and it settles. Horizontal or vertical, drag or hover, and the arrow on the stage is the library's own User Cursor demonstrating the drag until a real hand arrives.
reducedMotion: The divider keeps working and stops being thrown: no spring, no tour, no transitions - a drag puts the line exactly under the pointer. The comparison is the content, so switching it off would be switching the entry off; what goes is the motion, not the function.
brandNotes:
A rebuild, not a port. The idea comes from React Bits Pro, whose source is paid and gated and whose licence (2.4) forbids putting the Product in a repository or making it available to third parties; this repo is public and ships dist/ as a reusable bundle, so no Pro source may enter it. Nothing was copied - the clip, the spring, the tour and the knob are written here, and sourceUrl points at the docs page for provenance only.

Three decisions are load-bearing. The arrow is the library's User Cursor, mounted, because the standing rule is that any entry whose point is a pointer demonstrates it with that one arrow - a second hand-drawn cursor is what makes two cards look like two libraries. The divider stops short of both ends by default (`bounds`, in px): the frame clips, so a knob taken to the very edge renders as a half circle, and a half circle is not an approved Continia shape - the stop is dropped automatically when there is no knob to protect. And the frame takes the hub's own 15px tile radius rather than a radius of its own, because a media frame is the same family as the video-asset tiles.

height.note: the stage. Both hosts clamp a component's mount to the card, so this only bites when the entry is used on its own.

orientation.note: which way the divider runs. Everything else - the clip, the hit test, the keyboard, the labels - reads this one value, so there is no second vertical code path to keep in step.

initial.note: where the divider starts, 0-100. Clamped by `bounds` like every other position.

inertia.note: the divider is pulled to the pointer by a spring rather than written to it. Off, the line sits exactly under the pointer - which is what you want when a comparison is being measured rather than shown.

follow.note: the spring's time constant, off the duration scale. Bigger is heavier and later. It is a critically damped spring, not a lag: a lag answers a jumped target with its highest speed in the first frame, so a thrown divider would leave at a sprint and crawl in.

mode.note: drag is press and move; hover follows the pointer with no press. Hover reads well in a hero where nobody is told there is anything to grab, and badly anywhere a visitor might scroll past.

handle.note: the knob. Off, the divider is a bare line and `bounds` is dropped, so it reaches both edges.

grip.note: the six dots in the knob. Drawn as one dot and five shadows rather than six elements.

bounds.note: how close to the ends the divider may come. In px, not percent, so a 350px card and a 1200px hero keep the same visual gap. It exists because the frame clips: at 0 the knob renders as a half circle at each end, which is not an approved shape.

labels.note: two, comma separated; empty for none. Each one fades out as the divider reaches it - a label on the wrong side of the line sits over the other picture and stops saying anything.

cursor.note: mount the library's User Cursor and hand it the tour. Off, this is an ordinary slider waiting for a pointer.

name.note: the cursor's pill. Empty is the arrow on its own, which is what a slider wants - the pill is for a demo about a person.

cycle.note: one full tour: walk to the handle, press, drag to the before side, across to the after side, back to the middle, let go. A loop length, so an option rather than a token.

reach.note: how far either side of centre the tour drags, in percent. The tour deliberately does not run to the ends: a demo that empties the frame has nothing left to compare.

accent.note: the divider, the grip and the arrow. auto follows --navy, so Tech Blue on a light ground and Innovation Blue on a dark one.

autoplay.note: run once it scrolls into view, and stop again when it leaves or the tab is hidden

paused.note: stops the TOUR, not the component: a visitor can still drag the divider on a paused card, and the spring runs for that drag.

compact.note: the card-sized skin, for a stage under ~200px

notPorted: No stepped or snapping positions. A slider that clicks into thirds is a different control - it says the comparison has named states - and nothing in the hub has them. `set(n)` takes any position, so a caller who wants steps can round.
No more than two sides. A third layer needs two dividers and a rule for what happens when they cross, and at a card's width three strips of picture read as stripes rather than as a comparison.

No automatic image preloading. Both sides are the caller's markup, so an that has not decoded is the caller's to handle with loading/decoding attributes - adding a loader here would mean this entry deciding when someone else's picture is ready.
